name: secret_dependent_table_lookup
source_inspiration: Table-driven cryptographic implementations such as AES T-tables use secret-dependent values to index memory tables; cache attacks can observe which cache sets were touched.
representative_sources: Osvik, Shamir, and Tromer, Cache attacks and countermeasures: the case of AES
Bonneau and Mironov, Cache-collision timing attacks against AES

name: multi_table_lookup_footprint
source_inspiration: AES-style table-driven code often performs multiple table-like memory accesses during one sensitive operation, creating a wider secret-dependent cache footprint than a single lookup.
representative_sources: Osvik, Shamir, and Tromer, Cache attacks and countermeasures: the case of AES
Bonneau and Mironov, Cache-collision timing attacks against AES
simplified_pseudocode: for t in tables: access(table_base[t] + f(secret, t) * line_size)

name: secret_dependent_branch_footprint
source_inspiration: Constant-time guidance and cache-side-channel analysis identify secret-dependent branches/control flow as a leakage source when different branch paths touch different cache lines.
representative_sources: Constant-time cryptography guidance: avoid secret-dependent branches and memory accesses
Recent LLC Prime+Probe work against ECDSA-style code paths

name: secret_dependent_loop_count
source_inspiration: Variable-time secret-dependent control flow can change how many memory locations are touched; the cache footprint size can leak secret-dependent information.
representative_sources: Constant-time cryptography guidance: avoid secret-dependent branches and variable memory-access behavior
Cache side-channel detection work that tracks secret-dependent memory traces
simplified_pseudocode: for i in range(secret + 1): access(base + i * line_size)

name: set_aliasing_table_lookup
source_inspiration: Prime+Probe observes cache-set disturbance rather than exact addresses. Different logical table entries can alias to the same observed set, producing partial rather than full leakage.
representative_sources: Prime+Probe LLC attacks monitor cache-set activity rather than exact victim addresses
Cache side-channel analysis literature on cache-set-level observation
simplified_pseudocode: access(table_base + secret * stride), where multiple secrets map to the same cache set
